implementationPlan.note:
MECHANISM RE-CONFIRMED, AND THE REOPEN'S DIAGNOSIS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.

Round 1 already established the structural argument (decide() is fire-and-forget; the click's act cannot await a detached chain; spendOffer's crypto.subtle.digest is a threadpool promise). QA's reopen accepted that and rejected the BOUND: ANSWER_DRAINS = 10 is a hop count at a 0ms fake advance, which buys ~0 wall clock. I measured that claim instead of taking it on trust.

MEASUREMENT METHOD. No disk mutation of the delivered file. I generated an instrumented COPY of the whole test at apps/control-room/.drill/measure.test.tsx (import paths rewritten, drain helpers replaced by a real-wall-clock drain that records ms and tick count per read, results appended to a temp JSONL), plus two out-of-tree vitest configs. Deleted at the end of the row; .drill/ is outside the lane's `src/**` include so it can never inflate a count line.

RESULTS.
- Single-file run, quiet host: 10/10 reads needed ZERO ticks. Confirms a green single-file run proves nothing here.
- Single-file run under 24 spinning node processes AND a concurrent full lane: still 0 ticks on 60/60 reads. Synthetic contention on an isolated run does NOT reproduce it.
- INSIDE a real 206-file control-room lane (the instrumented copy added to the include list), 5 runs, 2 of them under 16 CPU hogs, 50 drained reads total: maxTicks 1, nonzeroTicks 3/50, and the most expensive SINGLE real event-loop turn cost 24ms of wall clock.

That 24ms is the number the repair is sized against. A real turn under lane load can cost 24ms; ten microtask hops cost well under 1ms. The bound was ~3 orders of magnitude short.

FOREIGN RED BASELINE, disclosed not hidden. The concurrent-load runs red only OTHER files, all previously catalogued as this lane's load-flake population: cordum-app, deploy-target-form, goal-publish, goals-home (x3), project-manager-app, environment-variables-screen. live-goal-release.test.tsx was NOT among them in any of those runs. One foreign red is worth naming because it is a different class: goals-home printed `expected 'hSihnidp bstadrieor ecnrtrdyentiS...' to be 'Ship stdio entry'` -- interleaved characters from two overlapping fireEvent.change sequences. Not mine, not in scope, and only visible under 24 hogs plus a concurrent lane.

Both target files were CLEAN at step start (`git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` listed only the three peer-dirty files approve-plan-reject.test.tsx, approve-plan.test.tsx, plan-run-resolution.test.tsx). Not touched. full-suite-gate acquired at 11:22Z for the lane runs.

DRAIN REBOUNDED ON REAL WALL CLOCK. Test-only. +70/-30 in one file; typecheck exit 0; file alone 1 passed (1) / 4 passed (4).

I DEVIATE FROM THIS STEP'S LITERAL INSTRUCTION AND SAY SO OPENLY. The step says "USE THE FILE'S OWN settle()". Round 1 did exactly that -- ten iterations of settle() behind ANSWER_DRAINS -- and QA red it twice in four lane runs. The step text predates the reopen; the reopen supersedes it on this exact point. `settle()` is `act(async () => vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0))`, so N of them buy ~0 wall clock, and the work being waited for resolves off Node's threadpool. Ten hops was ~3 orders of magnitude short of the 24ms a single real turn costs under lane load (step 1 measurement). Everything else the step mandates is kept: the repair is in the shared helper, not at a call site; no production edit; `findByTestId`/`waitFor` still rejected for the fake-timer hang; the drain is NOT inside confirmRelease().

WHAT SHIPPED.
- `realSetTimeout` / `realNow`: real `setTimeout` and real `Date.now` captured at MODULE LOAD, before beforeEach installs fake timers. Immune to whatever vi.useFakeTimers() replaces, and to any future change of its toFake set.
- `DRAIN_BUDGET_MS = 2_500`, with `drainBudgetLeftMs` reset in the existing beforeEach. Sized at ~100x the worst measured single turn (24ms).
- `drainTick()`: ONE real event-loop turn (`realSetTimeout(resolve, 1)` so libuv can deliver a threadpool completion in the poll phase) then `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)`, both inside `act`. Returns the real ms it consumed.
- `drainUntil(ready)`: spends turns until ready() or the budget is gone, then returns and lets the caller's own read produce the failure.
- `noteCode` and `sendCount` now call `drainUntil`. All five call sites (answerCode x4, readRefusalCode, sendCount x4) inherit it unchanged -- no call-site edits.

THREE DELIBERATE CHOICES A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK.
1. `Math.max(realNow() - startedAt, 1)` in drainTick. Without the floor, a turn the clock reports as 0ms would decrement nothing and `drainUntil` would spin FOREVER on a never-arriving answer -- turning the flake into a hang, which is precisely the failure mode the reopen told me to preserve against. The floor guarantees termination in at most DRAIN_BUDGET_MS ticks.
2. The budget is PER ARM, not per read, reset in beforeEach. Per-read at 2500ms would let one arm with three failing reads spend 7.5s and blow vitest's 5s per-test default, converting a fast RTL error into a slow timeout. Per-arm caps the total at 2.5s and keeps ~2.5s of headroom.
3. The FAKE clock still advances 0ms per tick, so no arm's 5s read poll fires as a side effect of looking -- the property the old settle()-based drain had and the arm at :148 depends on.

Line count 408 (was 368). Over the 400 soft cap by 8 lines; the rail scopes that cap to production sources and this is a test, but I trimmed ~14 lines of now-duplicated rationale to keep it close.
